speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you were involved in a rear-end collision and are experiencing right groin pain with abnormal leg positioning. Can you describe exactly how your leg is positioned and whether you are able to bear any weight on it?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient was involved in a rear-end collision where she was the restrained driver of the back car. She reports immediate onset of pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin area following the accident.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. Can you tell me if your right leg appears shorter than the left, or if it is rotated outward (externally rotated)? Also, on a scale of 1 to 10, how would you rate the pain in your right groin right now?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Severe right groin pain. I also have Pain in both knees, Right leg is slightly shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated.

speaker: Doctor
text: The position of your leg—shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated—is highly characteristic of a posterior hip dislocation. To confirm this and rule out associated fractures, I need to visualize the joint. REQUEST TEST: Pelvis_X-Ray
